target: Man ska vara försiktig på isen nu.
english: One should be careful on the ice now.
tip: Man is the impersonal one or people in general: Man ska vara försiktig = one should be careful.

target: Hon måste ringa tillbaka på kvällen nu.
english: She has to call back in the evening.
tip: tillbaka (back) is a particle: ringa tillbaka = call back.

target: Det brukar ta ungefär tjugo minuter att gå.
english: It usually takes approximately twenty minutes to walk.
tip: Brukar marks a habit, something usually done: det brukar ta = it usually takes.

target: Den svarta katten sitter i fönstret på jobbet.
english: The black cat sits in the window at work.
tip: Double definite with en-word: den + svarta + katten. Adjective always ends in -a in definite.

target: Vi har ingen aning om vad som hände efter festen.
english: We have no idea what happened after the party.
tip: When 'what' is the subject of an indirect clause, add som: vad som hände = what happened.

target: Hon vattnar blommorna.
english: She waters the flowers.
tip: En-words ending in -a form the definite plural with -orna: blomma becomes blommorna, the flowers.

target: Potatismos till köttbullarna.
english: Mashed potatoes with the meatballs.
tip: Till pairs a side with a dish, meaning to go with: potatismos till köttbullarna.

target: Fiskgratängen är husets specialitet.
english: The fish gratin is the house specialty.
tip: The genitive just adds -s, no apostrophe: husets specialitet = the house's specialty.

target: De svenska somrarna är korta.
english: The Swedish summers are short.
tip: Sommar has an irregular plural: en sommar, flera somrar, de somrarna, the summers.

target: Flickan med det röda håret.
english: The girl with the red hair.
tip: "Hår" is ett-word: "det röda håret" – double definite with adjective.

target: Var försiktig på vägen, det kan vara halt.
english: Be careful on the road, it can be slippery.
tip: Var is the imperative of vara (to be): Var försiktig = Be careful.

target: Jag skickade paketet med posten tidigt på måndagsmorgonen.
english: I sent the package by mail early on Monday morning.
tip: med can mean 'by means of': med posten = by mail.

target: Skit samma, vi gör det på vårt sätt istället.
english: Whatever, we will do it our way instead.
tip: Skit samma is a crude, slangy way to say 'whatever'. Keep it for casual speech only.

target: De samlade ihop pengar och köpte en gemensam present.
english: They collected money and bought a joint present.
tip: ihop = together, used as a particle: samlade ihop pengar = collected money.

target: Passa dig, det var verkligen oväntat men väldigt positivt!
english: Take care of yourself, it was really unexpected but very positive!
tip: passa sig means watch out, and it is reflexive: Passa dig.

target: Hon bakade en tårta till sin dotters födelsedag igår.
english: She baked a cake for her daughter's birthday yesterday.
tip: You can stack sin with a genitive: sin dotters födelsedag = her own daughter's birthday.

target: Han började jobba tidigt och slutade sent varje dag förut.
english: He started working early and finished late every day before.
tip: After börja, att before the next verb is optional: började jobba = started working.

target: Hon målade om hela sovrummet i en vacker blå färg.
english: She repainted the whole bedroom in a beautiful blue color.
tip: As a particle, om can mean 're-' or 'again': måla om = repaint.

target: Jag lyssnade på henne medan hon berättade om sin barndom.
english: I listened to her while she told about her childhood.
tip: lyssna på = listen to; the på is required: jag lyssnade på henne.

target: Vilken otur att det började regna precis när vi kom.
english: How unfortunate that it started raining just when we arrived.
tip: vilken/vilket plus a noun makes an exclamation: Vilken otur = what bad luck.

target: Det vore trevligt om du kunde hjälpa mig med det.
english: It would be nice if you could help me with that.
tip: vore is the 'would be' form of vara, for hypotheticals: det vore trevligt = it would be nice.

target: Jag sprang till bussen men hann inte med den tyvärr.
english: I ran to the bus but missed it, unfortunately.
tip: hinna med = manage to catch in time: hann inte med den = didn't make it.

target: Det var länge sedan jag pratade svenska med någon annan.
english: It was a long time since I spoke Swedish with someone else.
tip: det var länge sedan = it's been a long time since: länge sedan jag pratade svenska.

target: Duktig som hon är löser hon allt.
english: Skilled as she is, she solves everything.
tip: Adjective fronting for emphasis: adjective + som + subject + verb.

target: Stäng fönstret.
english: Close the window.
tip: Swedish commands drop the subject: stäng is just the bare verb, no 'du'. Stäng fönstret (Close the window).

target: Det gör inget.
english: It doesn't matter.
tip: Det gör inget is a set phrase for 'it doesn't matter', literally 'it does nothing'.

target: Ta det lugnt.
english: Take it easy.
tip: As an adverb here, lugn takes the neuter -t: lugnt. Ta det lugnt is the fixed phrase for 'take it easy'.

target: Räkorna är färska.
english: The shrimp are fresh.
tip: En-words ending in -a form the definite plural with -orna: räka becomes räkorna (the shrimp).

target: Han rastar hunden.
english: He walks the dog.
tip: Rasta specifically means to walk or exercise an animal: Han rastar hunden (He walks the dog).

target: Övergångsstället är framme.
english: The crosswalk is up ahead.
tip: Framme means already there or up ahead at a spot; fram is for motion toward: Övergångsstället är framme.
